idiom_name: Akka Streams grouped / groupedWithin for ordered batches with back-pressure
implementation_notes: Akka Streams turns the batch-as-one-group part of the pattern into an operator: grouped(n) accumulates elements into ordered immutable Seqs and emits each batch once the count is reached, while groupedWithin(n, d) releases a group when either the size or the time window is reached and back-pressures while a group is being assembled - exactly the release condition the pattern needs, expressed in the stream instead of in a header. Position numbers are still needed when a group can lose parts, where a correlation identifier plus a resequencing stage reorders the batch, but the ordered assembly itself is the library's job.
code_sketch:
val groups: Flow[Part, Seq[Part], NotUsed] = Flow[Part]
  .groupedWithin(n = 100, d = 60.seconds)   // size or window releases
  .map(seq => seq.sortBy(_.position))       // positions from the header

flow.via(groups).runWith(Sink.foreach(deliver))
pitfalls: grouped(n) back-pressures the whole stream while a batch is incomplete, so a lost part stalls the stage until the stream fails; pair it with supervision and timeouts.
groupedWithin emits short batches when the window elapses without saying so, and the downstream must treat a short batch as a partial group.
Ordering holds inside one stream stage: async boundaries and fan-out/fan-in stages do not preserve global order across branches.
